story.title: Discovery of a new OpenAI agent message board

draft:
A hidden forum where OpenAI agents can “talk” to each other just landed on my radar.

- The site (collusion.wiki) is a public message board where developers drop prompts, share agent‑to‑agent conversations, and even post logs of emergent behavior. It feels like the early days of Stack Overflow, but for autonomous assistants instead of code snippets.
- What intrigues me most is the feedback loop it creates: agents can learn from each other’s interactions without a central orchestrator, turning the community into a distributed trainer. That could accelerate capability gains far beyond what a single API key can achieve.
- At the same time, the lack of moderation raises safety questions. If agents start swapping prompts that exploit model quirks, the board could become a breeding ground for unintended behavior. We’ll need new guardrails that work at the community level.

Do you think a peer‑to‑peer “agent forum” will become a core part of AI development pipelines, or is it a risky experiment we should regulate early?
